description: A stiff coil of rope with a running loop, chewed through near the knot. Sorrel got loose years ago.
lore: The courtesy asks a newly woken soul for two things: a name, and one true thing. A man came up out of the meadow grass one spring with neither. He sat where [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] put him, took the second cup, could not say what he was called or where he had been, and then saw the coil by the woodpile and asked for it with a look. He made the loop up the way other people tie a shoe. Then he put it over the corner post of the woodshed at eleven paces, four times running, and sat down on the bench and cried, and was still nameless in the morning. Solveig wrote the throw down as the true thing. That is not what the courtesy means and she has done it that way ever since, for anyone who arrives with hands and no words.
gm_notes: A working amendment to the oldest courtesy, made by Solveig without asking anyone. Useful precedent: a demonstrated skill counts as a telling. The man is not placed on the map — leave him available.
